style: requiem-dark hospital emergency underscore, fourteen seconds, dialogue scene not a song: a bass choir of men holding one closed-mouth note like a cathedral at midnight, pipe organ sixteen-foot pedal tone shaking the floor, an ambulance siren whooping and climbing with the choir, downpour hammering a van roof; every line is yelled and talked, no melody on the words, the people sit on top of the music; at the stop the choir cuts and a single choirboy, small, timid and alone, sings three falling notes with no words, again and again, while a cold patrician gentleman grumbles faintly through a sealed window; then nothing but one flat monitor beep held long, then total silence
exclude: upbeat, cheerful, comedic, pop, rap, hip-hop, drums, beat, rhyme, chorus hook, anthem, sung words, melodic yelling, female choir, trailer braams, reverb tail, fade-out, outro
lyrics:
[Intro: bass choir hum, organ pedal, siren climbing, heavy rain]
[Spoken Word, screaming, gravel-voiced woman in her fifties]
(Sixty over thirty! Fucking hurry up, we're gonna lose him!)
[Spoken Word, panting young man, voice breaking]
(Sats dropping, he's peri-arrest!)
[Yelled, enraged driver, mouth wide open]
(TWO MINUTES OUT! GET THE FUCK OUT OF THE WAY!)

[Break: siren cuts, choir cuts, lone choirboy, three falling notes, no words, repeating]
[Spoken Word, young man, lost and frightened]
(Why have we stopped?!)
[Spoken Word, faint, icy upper-class gent, through a closed car window]
(I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!)

[Outro: all music gone, woman barely audible]
(Fifty over twen—)
[Single flat heart monitor tone]
[Silence]
[End]
title: PL r3-child-and-choir
